title: Molecular characterization of a rare norovirus GII.8[P8] strain detected during pediatric acute gastroenteritis surveillance in Harbin, China
abstract: Norovirus is a major causative agent of pediatric acute gastroenteritis, whereas GII.8[P8] represents a rare, non-dominant genotype with limited publicly available whole-genome data. We characterized a GII.8[P8] norovirus strain, Harbin-Nov-076-2022, detected through routine surveillance of pediatric acute gastroenteritis in Harbin, China. The strain was obtained from a stool sample of a 15-month-old female patient and subjected to whole-genome sequencing using the DNBSEQ-T7 platform. Integrated analyses included phylogenetic reconstruction, amino acid entropy profiling, selection pressure assessment, homology modeling of the capsid P protein, and B-cell epitope prediction. The near-complete genome of Harbin-Nov-076-2022 is 7486 nt in length, with a GC content of 53.81%, and displays the canonical three-open-reading-frame organization of human noroviruses. The sequence was deposited in GenBank under accession number PV416744. Phylogenetic analysis assigned the strain to the GII.8[P8] lineage, with the highest nucleotide identity of 97.52% to the Thai 2018 strain GII/Hu/TH/2018/GII.8[P8]/B6213 (ACCN: OR546393). Amino acid variability was highest in the VP2 region, with three variable sites (residues 15, 122, and 229) identified among the aligned GII.8[P8] VP2 sequences, whereas selection pressure analysis indicated that the genome was largely constrained by purifying selection. Same-template P-domain modeling predicted localized sequence-associated variations in the P2 subdomain and HBGA-binding-associated surface loops, with 59 predicted B-cell epitopes. These findings expand whole-genome evidence for rare GII.8[P8] norovirus in Northeast China and provide regional genomic data for molecular surveillance, evolutionary assessment, and antigenic characterization of non-dominant norovirus genotypes.

title: Zymosan-adjuvanted intranasal norovirus virus-like particle vaccine induces antiviral mucosal immune responses in infant mice.
abstract: Infants require repeated immunizations of injectable-type vaccines against different pathogens because their immune systems are weaker than those of adults. However, these injectable vaccines cause physical and psychological discomfort. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop pain-free mucosal vaccines that are optimized for immunologically immature infants. Using an infant murine model, we examined the effectiveness of an intranasal norovirus virus-like-particle (VLP) vaccine with zymosan as an adjuvant. The intranasal immunization of infant mice with VLPs alone induced mucosal and systemic VLP-specific immune responses that were substantially weaker than those of adults. In contrast, infant mice administered a minimum dose of intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, at levels comparable to those in adults. Importantly, intestinal and salivary antibodies elicited by intranasal immunization with the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine effectively inhibited norovirus propagation in human-induced pluripotent stem cellderived intestinal epithelial cells. These findings suggest that the intranasal zymosan-adjuvanted norovirus VLP vaccine is an effective mucosal vaccine candidate for infants. It may help reduce the pain associated with injections and the number of immunizations infants required to achieve sufficient protective immunity against norovirus.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for pain-free mucosal vaccines optimized for infants, as their immune systems are weaker than adults, necessitating repeated immunizations with injectable vaccines that cause discomfort.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used an infant murine model to examine the effectiveness of an intranasal norovirus virus-like-particle (VLP) vaccine with zymosan as an adjuvant.
analysis.methods: The researchers administered the vaccine to infant mice and measured immune responses, including levels of VLP-specific IgA antibodies in intestinal and salivary tissues, as well as VLP-specific IgG antibodies in plasma.
analysis.main_results: Infant mice given a minimum dose of the zymosan-adjuvanted VLP vaccine showed increased levels of intestinal and salivary VLP-specific IgA antibodies, as well as plasma VLP-specific IgG antibodies, comparable to those in adults.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the zymosan-adjuvanted norovirus VLP vaccine can induce effective mucosal immune responses in infants, potentially reducing the need for painful injections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform the development of mucosal vaccines for infants, offering a non-invasive alternative to injectable vaccines and improving compliance with immunization schedules.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an infant murine model, which may not fully represent human immune responses, but the evidence is strong due to direct comparisons with adult responses and biological relevance.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of a zymosan-adjuvanted intranasal norovirus virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine to induce mucosal immune responses in infant mice. The research was motivated by the need for pain-free and effective vaccines for infants, as their immune systems are less mature and injectable vaccines are uncomfortable. The study used an infant murine model to evaluate the vaccine's effectiveness, finding that it induced immune responses comparable to those in adults. These results suggest that the vaccine could be a promising candidate for infant immunization against norovirus, potentially reducing the need for multiple painful injections. The findings have implications for developing non-invasive vaccines for infants, which could improve immunization compliance and effectiveness. However, the study's reliance on a murine model limits the direct applicability of the results to humans, though the evidence is strong and relevant.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在满足婴幼儿对无痛黏膜型疫苗的需求,因其免疫系统较成年人薄弱,需反复接种引发不适的针剂型疫苗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用婴幼鼠模型,探究以酵母聚糖为佐剂的鼻喷诺如病毒病毒样颗粒(VLP)疫苗的免疫效果。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员向婴幼鼠接种疫苗,并检测免疫应答,包括肠道和唾液组织中VLP特异性IgA抗体水平,以及血浆中VLP特异性IgG抗体水平。
elements_zh.main_results: 接种最低剂量酵母聚糖佐剂化VLP 疫苗的婴幼鼠,其肠道和唾液中VLP特异性IgA抗体水平,以及血浆中VLP特异性IgG抗体水平,均与成年鼠相当。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,酵母聚糖佐剂化诺如病毒 VLP 疫苗可在婴幼儿中诱导有效的黏膜型免疫应答,有望减少疼痛注射的需求。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为婴幼儿黏膜型疫苗的开发提供参考,为注射型疫苗提供非侵入性替代方案,并提高免疫接种依从性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于婴幼鼠模型,可能无法完全代表人类免疫应答,但通过与成年鼠反应的直接对比及生物学相关性,证据强度较高。

title: Norovirus on Cruise Ships: A Recurring Sentinel Event
abstract: Norovirus remains the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis outbreaks worldwide and is particularly well adapted for transmission aboard cruise ships due to its low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and rapid person-to-person spread. We reviewed recent outbreaks to highlight recurring norovirus outbreaks and gaps in maritime surveillance. These demonstrate the vulnerability of cruise ships to rapid viral amplification and international dissemination. Current surveillance relies predominantly on symptomatic case reporting, limiting the ability to distinguish between single-source introduction, environmental persistence, foodborne transmission, and emergence of novel recombinant strains. Recent modelling studies have shown that early diagnosis and isolation of symptomatic individuals substantially reduce secondary transmission, yet routine genomic surveillance is rarely implemented onboard. Wastewater-based surveillance offers a practical, non-invasive early warning approach that can be integrated into existing ship infrastructure and complemented by genomic sequencing to identify circulating variants and transmission pathways. Incorporating molecular and wastewater surveillance into routine maritime health programmes would strengthen outbreak detection, improve infection control, and enhance global preparedness for recurrent norovirus outbreaks associated with international cruise travel.

The evidence base includes recent outbreaks and modeling studies, which emphasize the need for improved surveillance and infection control measures. media_mentions.content: Abstract Norovirus remains the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis outbreaks worldwide and is particularly well adapted for transmission aboard cruise ships due to its low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and rapid person-to-person spread. We reviewed recent outbreaks to highlight recurring norovirus outbreaks and gaps in maritime surveillance. These demonstrate the vulnerability of cruise ships to rapid viral amplification and international dissemination. Current surveillance relies predominantly on symptomatic case reporting, limiting the ability to distinguish between single-source introduction, environmental persistence, foodborne transmission, and emergence of novel recombinant strains. Recent modelling studies have shown that early diagnosis and isolation of symptomatic individuals substantially reduce secondary transmission, yet routine genomic surveillance is rarely implemented onboard. Wastewater-based surveillance offers a practical, non-invasive early warning approach that can be integrated into existing ship infrastructure and complemented by genomic sequencing to identify circulating variants and transmission pathways. Incorporating molecular and wastewater surveillance into routine maritime health programmes would strengthen outbreak detection, improve infection control, and enhance global preparedness for recurrent norovirus outbreaks associated with international cruise travel. Editorial In 2026, three significant norovirus outbreaks were reported aboard the Star Princess, Caribbean Princess, and Ambition between March and May 2026 [1-3]. However, despite recurrent outbreaks, cruise ships continue to be potent amplification environments for norovirus transmission. However, genomic surveillance and outbreak tracking remain restricted [4,5]. This indicates a persistent gap in global maritime infectious disease surveillance, highlighting this continuing public health challenge. The outbreaks on the three cruise ships highlight how quickly enteric viruses like norovirus can disseminate across international travel networks once introduced into confined maritime settings (Table 1, Figure 1). During a seven-day voyage (March 7-14, 2026), the Star Princess recorded 193 cases of gastrointestinal illness among 5,868 passengers and crew, with a 3.29% attack rate. The United States Vessel Sanitation Program was notified on March 11, 2026 [1]. The Caribbean Princess, which departed Port Everglades on April 28, 2026, reported 160 cases of gastrointestinal illness during its 13-day Southern Caribbean voyage among 4,247 passengers and crew, corresponding to a 3.77% attack rate [2]. The Ambition, operated by Ambassador Cruise Line, departed Belfast on May 8, 2026, for a 14-night voyage to France and Spain. The vessel carried 1,187 passengers and 514 crew members (1,701 total). After arriving in Bordeaux, French authorities temporarily restricted disembarkation because of an outbreak of gastrointestinal illness. As of May 14, 2026, 60 passengers and four crew members were reported to be experiencing gastrointestinal illness, and laboratory testing confirmed norovirus [3]. Norovirus is uniquely adapted for transmission aboard cruise ships. Its very low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, resistance to commonly used disinfectants, and efficient aerosolisation during vomiting make it particularly suited to cruise ship environments [2,5]. Hundreds of passengers share ventilation systems, dining halls, recreational facilities, and semi-enclosed cabin corridors for prolonged periods. The CDC Vessel Sanitation Program continues to document recurrent gastrointestinal illness outbreaks aboard cruise ships, with norovirus identified as the causative agent in many reported events [6]. Regular handwashing, thorough cooking of shellfish, proper washing of fresh produce, and disinfection of contaminated surfaces are recommended preventive measures against norovirus [6]. Recent modelling studies further highlight the importance of early case identification and isolation during norovirus outbreaks aboard cruise ships. Analysis of seven Mediterranean cruise outbreaks involving 359 cases demonstrated that isolation of diagnosed individuals immediately upon symptoms reduced their transmissibility by approximately 94% under the study conditions. The same modelling framework improved forecasts compared with a baseline model, with improvement observed for 78% of data points at forecasting horizons longer than 72 hours [7]. These findings support rapid diagnosis and cabin isolation as important outbreak-control measures while also illustrating how mathematical modelling can complement routine syndromic surveillance. There are still significant gaps in outbreak surveillance. Most cruise ships continue to rely primarily on symptomatic passengers reporting to onboard medical services, a strategy that frequently detects outbreaks only after substantial transmission has already occurred [8]. Routine sequencing of norovirus strains is rarely performed onboard, making it difficult to distinguish between single-source introduction, ongoing environmental contamination, foodborne transmission, and the emergence of novel recombinant variants. Genomic surveillance could additionally help track inter-voyage viral spread across ports and identify globally circulating strains associated with repeated maritime outbreaks [5]. This limitation has important public health implications. During outbreaks at sea, clinicians cannot readily determine whether cases result from a single introduction, ongoing environmental contamination, foodborne transmission, or the emergence of a new variant. Syndromic surveillance alone is insufficient to distinguish between these scenarios, although each requires different public health interventions [4,5,8]. Wastewater-based surveillance offers a practical solution. It requires no active passenger participation, can be integrated into existing ship infrastructure, and has already proven valuable as an early-warning tool during the COVID-19 pandemic. Wastewater surveillance could serve as a complementary, non-invasive early-warning approach on cruise ships and could be paired with genomic sequencing to characterize circulating norovirus strains. Passive wastewater sampling has been explored as a scalable infectious-disease surveillance strategy, including during the COVID-19 pandemic [9]. Such an approach could enable earlier detection while complementing, rather than replacing, clinical surveillance. Despite growing global attention to marine health security, these approaches remain largely absent from routine cruise ship operations. Integrating syndromic surveillance with targeted wastewater-based molecular detection and genomic sequencing could provide a more comprehensive approach to maritime infectious-disease surveillance. The objective should not be to create an entirely new surveillance system onboard every vessel, but to complement existing medical reporting and sanitation systems with targeted molecular surveillance that is feasible, scalable, and linked to established public health response pathways. Such integration could facilitate earlier recognition of outbreaks, improve understanding of transmission, and strengthen preparedness for recurrent norovirus events associated with international cruise travel. title: Treatment With Ruxolitinib and TAK-779 Enhances GII.17 Human Norovirus Replication and Enables Serial Passaging in Human Intestinal Enteroids.
abstract: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs. TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.
journal: Genes to cells : devoted to molecular & cellular mechanisms

title: Clinical characteristics associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with laboratory-confirmed norovirus gastroenteritis
abstract: Introduction Norovirus (NoV) is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis in children, but pathogen-confirmed data in neonates remain limited, particularly regarding clinical differences associated with gastrointestinal bleeding. Methods We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of neonates younger than 28 days who were hospitalized at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University between December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, had positive stool NoV antigen results, and underwent confirmatory nucleic acid testing. After excluding clinically identifiable alternative causes of gastrointestinal bleeding, patients were classified into hemorrhagic and non-hemorrhagic groups. Baseline characteristics, clinical manifestations, comorbidities, and laboratory findings obtained within 24 h after admission were compared between groups. Laboratory variables showing significant between-group differences were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model. Results A total of 139 neonates were included, comprising 52 in the hemorrhagic group and 87 in the non-hemorrhagic group. Among the hemorrhagic cases, 49 had overt gastrointestinal bleeding and three had isolated fecal occult blood positivity. The hemorrhagic group had a higher frequency of diarrhea and a lower frequency of jaundice. Hemoglobin, total bilirubin, indirect bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, the aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio, pH-corrected venous ionized calcium, chloride, and lactate were lower in the hemorrhagic group, whereas blood base excess was higher. In multivariable logistic regression, each 0.1 mmol/L increase in ionized calcium was associated with lower odds of the hemorrhagic phenotype (OR = 0.624, 95% CI: 0.410–0.950; P = 0.028). Discussion Neonates with laboratory-confirmed NoV gastroenteritis showed different clinical and laboratory characteristics according to the presence of gastrointestinal bleeding. The association with lower ionized calcium should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design and potential residual confounding.

A single-center retrospective observational study was conducted on 139 neonates hospitalized between December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2025, at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University. title: Emergence of a novel GII.17 variant is associated with immune evasion rather than an altered HBGA-binding profile
abstract: The epidemiology of noroviruses, a major cause of gastroenteritis in humans, is shaped by their continuous evolution. Novel genotypes and variants periodically emerge, replacing previously dominant strains. In 2024, a novel GII.17 variant led to an increased number of notified outbreaks, becoming the dominant genotype detected in Europe. To investigate if this surge in GII.17 detection is attributable to changes in binding and antigenicity of this novel variant, we compared properties of a GII.17 2024 strain with representative GII.17 strains from 2005 (Clade B), 2014 (Clade C), and 2015 (Clade D), and the epidemic GII.4 Sydney 2012 variant. Norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) were used to assess binding to saliva samples and human intestinal tissues with different histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) profiles. Binding specificity to individual glycans was determined using synthetic HBGAs. Additionally, VP1-NanoLuc (NLuc) fusion proteins were used in binding blocking assays to evaluate the antigenic properties of the variants using 75 sera from healthy adults that were collected during different time periods of GII.17 circulation (the winters of 2009–2010, 2015 and 2024). Compared with other GII.17 variants, the 2024 strain exhibits amino acid substitutions in the P2 domain, which contains both antigenic sites and the HBGA binding site. Binding-blocking assays with human sera confirmed that the 2024 variant is antigenically distinct from the 2005 and 2015 GII.17 strains but closely related to the 2014 variant. All post-2005 GII.17 strains showed a broader HBGA binding profile compared to the GII.17 2005 strain, likely contributing to their more successful spread. These findings show that the recent re-emergence of GII.17 coincided with antigenic drift, enabling it to escape from pre-existing immunity, but not with major changes in HBGA binding specificity. Understanding the factors influencing norovirus emergence is essential for the development of preventive strategies against future norovirus epidemics.

Novel genotypes and variants periodically emerge, replacing previously dominant strains. In 2024, a novel GII.17 variant led to an increased number of notified outbreaks, becoming the dominant genotype detected in Europe. To investigate if this surge in GII.17 detection is attributable to changes in binding and antigenicity of this novel variant, we compared properties of a GII.17 2024 strain with representative GII.17 strains from 2005 (Clade B), 2014 (Clade C), and 2015 (Clade D), and the epidemic GII.4 Sydney 2012 variant. Norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) were used to assess binding to saliva samples and human intestinal tissues with different histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) profiles. Binding specificity to individual glycans was determined using synthetic HBGAs. Additionally, VP1-NanoLuc (NLuc) fusion proteins were used in binding blocking assays to evaluate the antigenic properties of the variants using 75 sera from healthy adults that were collected during different time periods of GII.17 circulation (the winters of 2009–2010, 2015 and 2024). Compared with other GII.17 variants, the 2024 strain exhibits amino acid substitutions in the P2 domain, which contains both antigenic sites and the HBGA binding site. Binding-blocking assays with human sera confirmed that the 2024 variant is antigenically distinct from the 2005 and 2015 GII.17 strains but closely related to the 2014 variant. All post-2005 GII.17 strains showed a broader HBGA binding profile compared to the GII.17 2005 strain, likely contributing to their more successful spread. These findings show that the recent re-emergence of GII.17 coincided with antigenic drift, enabling it to escape from pre-existing immunity, but not with major changes in HBGA binding specificity. Understanding the factors influencing norovirus emergence is essential for the development of preventive strategies against future norovirus epidemics.

title_zh: 一种新型GII.17变异株的出现与其免疫逃逸能力相关,而非其组织血型抗原结合特性的改变
source_body_en: The epidemiology of noroviruses, a major cause of gastroenteritis in humans, is shaped by their continuous evolution. Novel genotypes and variants periodically emerge, replacing previously dominant strains. In 2024, a novel GII.17 variant led to an increased number of notified outbreaks, becoming the dominant genotype detected in Europe. To investigate if this surge in GII.17 detection is attributable to changes in binding and antigenicity of this novel variant, we compared properties of a GII.17 2024 strain with representative GII.17 strains from 2005 (Clade B), 2014 (Clade C), and 2015 (Clade D), and the epidemic GII.4 Sydney 2012 variant. Norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) were used to assess binding to saliva samples and human intestinal tissues with different histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) profiles. Binding specificity to individual glycans was determined using synthetic HBGAs. Additionally, VP1-NanoLuc (NLuc) fusion proteins were used in binding blocking assays to evaluate the antigenic properties of the variants using 75 sera from healthy adults that were collected during different time periods of GII.17 circulation (the winters of 2009–2010, 2015 and 2024). Compared with other GII.17 variants, the 2024 strain exhibits amino acid substitutions in the P2 domain, which contains both antigenic sites and the HBGA binding site. Binding-blocking assays with human sera confirmed that the 2024 variant is antigenically distinct from the 2005 and 2015 GII.17 strains but closely related to the 2014 variant. All post-2005 GII.17 strains showed a broader HBGA binding profile compared to the GII.17 2005 strain, likely contributing to their more successful spread. These findings show that the recent re-emergence of GII.17 coincided with antigenic drift, enabling it to escape from pre-existing immunity, but not with major changes in HBGA binding specificity. Understanding the factors influencing norovirus emergence is essential for the development of preventive strategies against future norovirus epidemics.
abstract_zh: 人诺如病毒(一种导致急性胃肠炎的主要病原体)的流行株谱受其持续进化驱动。新基因型和变异株会定期出现,并取代先前的优势株。2024年,一种新型GII.17变异株导致报告病例数量增加,成为欧洲检测到的优势基因型。为探究2024年GII.17检出激增是否归因于该新型变异株结合特性和抗原性的改变,研究者比较了2024年GII.17毒株与2005年(分支B)、2014年(分支C)、2015年(分支D)及流行GII.4悉尼2012变异株的性质。研究使用诺如病毒样颗粒(VLPs)评估其对不同组织血型抗原(HBGA)谱型唾液样本和人肠组织的结合能力,并通过合成HBGA确定其对单一糖类的结合特异性。此外,研究者构建了VP1-NanoLuc(NLuc)融合蛋白,通过结合阻断实验评估变异株的抗原性,所用75份健康成人血清采集自GII.17流行的不同时期(2009–2010、2015及2024年冬季)。与其他GII.17变异株相比,2024年毒株在P2结构域存在氨基酸替换,该区域同时包含抗原位点和HBGA结合位点。人血清结合阻断实验证实,2024年变异株在抗原性上与2005年和2015年GII.17毒株存在显著差异,但与2014年变异株高度相关。所有2005年后出现的GII.17毒株较2005年毒株显示出更广泛的HBGA结合谱,这可能有助于其更成功传播。研究结果表明,GII.17近期再次出现与抗原漂移相关,使其能够逃避既存免疫,但其HBGA结合特异性未发生重大改变。理解影响诺如病毒出现的因素对制定未来诺如病毒流行的预防策略至关重要。

title: Breastfeeding and viral infections in preterm infants: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of breastfeeding status up to 6 months of age on the incidence of viral infections during the first year of life in preterm infants. METHODS: Data were obtained from the Japanese National Hospital Organization Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Registry for the periods 2010-2014 and 2016-2018. Information on breastfeeding exposure and infection history was collected through parental questionnaires administered when the infants reached one year of age. A total of 3,368 preterm infants who completed follow-up at one year were analyzed. The risk ratio (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using a modified Poisson regression model to evaluate the association between breastfeeding and the risk of viral infections, including influenza virus, respiratory syncytial (RS) virus, rotavirus, and norovirus. RESULTS: Breastfeeding was associated with a lower risk of influenza infection (adjusted RR: 0.66, 95% CI: 0.48-0.89) and indicated a trend toward lower risk for other viral infections. CONCLUSION: Breastfeeding for up to 6 months may lower the risk of viral infections in preterm infants, suggesting that providing breastfeeding support could contribute to improved health outcomes. IMPACT: This study examined the association between breastfeeding up to 6 months and viral infections in preterm infants using data from a multicenter cohort. Breastfeeding was associated with a lower incidence of influenza and showed a possible protective association with other viral infections. These findings support the promotion of breastfeeding in preterm infants as part of infection prevention strategies. Given the vulnerability of preterm infants, further research is required to confirm these associations and to evaluate the long-term health implications of breastfeeding.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of breastfeeding on viral infections in preterm infants, focusing on norovirus and other related viruses. It used a multicenter cohort design, collecting data from the Japanese National Hospital Organization Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Registry between 2010-2014 and 2016-2018. Parental questionnaires were used to gather information on breastfeeding exposure and infection history, with 3,368 preterm infants included in the analysis. The study found that breastfeeding was associated with a lower risk of influenza infection and showed a trend toward lower risk for other viral infections, including norovirus. The authors suggest that breastfeeding support may improve health outcomes in preterm infants. However, they note the need for further research to confirm these associations and assess long-term implications. The evidence is moderate, as the study relies on self-reported data and does not account for all potential confounding factors.

title: Microbial assessment of recontamination with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter in patient room environment in a burn unit.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have demonstrated that environmental contamination with several epidemiologically important pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus spp, Acinetobacter, norovirus, and Clostridioides difficile, can persist for several days to months and contributes to the transmission of these pathogens. METHODS: This study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to determine the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with a multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. After disinfection, samples were taken from 6 environmental sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours. RESULTS: Time to recontamination with Acinetobacter was as follows: chair, 3 hours; overbed table, 2 hours; stock cabinet, 3 hours; and IV pump, 2 hours. CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated that recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly at environmental sites in burn units even after cleaning/disinfection and underscored the need for enhanced environmental cleaning, including continuous disinfection methods, to prevent transmission of health care-associated pathogens.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the persistent problem of environmental contamination by epidemiologically important pathogens in healthcare settings and sought to determine how quickly surfaces become recontaminated with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective observational study was conducted in a burn intensive care unit to measure the time to recontamination of environmental surfaces with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after routine disinfection.
analysis.methods: Environmental samples were collected from six specific sites using Rodac plates at 1-hour intervals for 10 hours following disinfection to assess recontamination dynamics.
analysis.main_results: Recontamination with Acinetobacter occurred rapidly, with positive samples detected at 2 hours on the overbed table and IV pump, and at 3 hours on the chair and stock cabinet.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that recontamination happens quickly even after cleaning, highlighting the need for enhanced environmental cleaning strategies, including continuous disinfection, to reduce transmission risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the importance of implementing more rigorous and continuous disinfection protocols in burn units to prevent healthcare-associated Acinetobacter transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a single burn unit and did not evaluate the effectiveness of specific disinfection methods or long-term outcomes, indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study in a burn intensive care unit assessed how quickly environmental surfaces become recontaminated with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii after disinfection. Sampling from six sites using Rodac plates at hourly intervals for 10 hours showed that recontamination occurred within 2 to 3 hours, with positive samples detected earliest on the overbed table and IV pump. The authors interpreted these results as evidence that routine cleaning is insufficient and that continuous disinfection is necessary to reduce transmission risks. The findings suggest that enhanced environmental cleaning protocols are urgently needed in burn units to prevent healthcare-associated Acinetobacter infections.

abstract_zh: 背景:大量研究表明,环境中多种流行病学重要病原体的污染,包括耐甲氧西林金黄色葡萄球菌、耐万古霉素肠球菌、不动杆菌、诺如病毒和艰难梭菌,可以持续数天至数月,并导致这些病原体的传播。方法:本研究在烧伤重症监护室进行,以确定消毒后环境表面被多重耐药鲍曼不动杆菌再次污染的时间。消毒后,使用Rodac板在6个环境点采样10小时,每隔1小时采样一次。结果:不动杆菌再次污染的时间如下:椅子,3小时;床头柜,2小时;库存柜,3小时;和 IV 泵,2 小时。结论:我们的研究表明,即使在清洁/消毒后,不动杆菌的再污染也会在烧伤单位的环境部位迅速发生,并强调需要加强环境清洁,包括持续消毒方法,以防止医疗保健相关病原体的 传播。

title: Evolution, diversity and distribution of human Noroviruses:From single hosts to global patterns
abstract: Norovirus, a member of the Caliciviridae family, is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, affecting all age groups and causing substantial morbidity and mortality. Children in developing countries, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals are particularly affected. Currently, no specific antivirals or vaccines are licensed for norovirus treatment or prevention. Therapeutic development is complicated by the virus's high diversity, with more than 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, some of which, such as GII.4, continuously generate new antigenic variants. However, the emergence of norovirus diversity, the relationship between within-host and community-level evolution, and the association between viral diversity and treatment outcome remain incompletely understood. Therefore, this thesis aims to improve our understanding of norovirus evolution and epidemiology by addressing two main topics: norovirus diversity and evolution in different hosts, and the use of wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus causes substantial global morbidity and mortality from acute gastroenteritis, yet key knowledge gaps persist regarding its high diversity, within-host and community-level evolution, and links between diversity and treatment outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This thesis synthesizes existing evidence to address norovirus diversity and epidemiology across hosts and populations, integrating host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing for population-level monitoring.
analysis.methods: The study employs a comparative and integrative approach, combining literature review with wastewater-based sequencing to examine viral diversity and circulation patterns at the population level.
analysis.main_results: The thesis identifies over 10 genogroups (GI–GX) and approximately 50 genotypes, with GII.4 continuously generating new antigenic variants, highlighting the virus's extensive diversity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work interprets the observed diversity as a driver of therapeutic challenges and proposes wastewater-based sequencing as a tool to monitor norovirus evolution and circulation, emphasizing the need to bridge within-host and community-level evolutionary insights.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance strategies and underscore the urgency for vaccine and antiviral development, given the absence of licensed options and the virus's antigenic variability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by its reliance on a literature-based synthesis and wastewater sequencing, which may not capture all host-specific dynamics or treatment associations, warranting moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis examines norovirus diversity and epidemiology to address critical gaps in understanding its evolution and public health impact. It synthesizes evidence showing norovirus as a major global cause of acute gastroenteritis, with over 10 genogroups and 50 genotypes, including the antigenically variable GII.4. The study integrates host-specific analyses and wastewater-based sequencing to monitor viral diversity and circulation at the population level. Key findings highlight the virus's extensive diversity as a barrier to therapeutic and vaccine development, with no licensed antivirals or vaccines currently available. The work interprets these patterns as evidence of ongoing antigenic drift and calls for improved surveillance and intervention strategies. Limitations include the reliance on literature synthesis and wastewater data, which may not fully capture host-specific dynamics or treatment outcomes, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

title: An Ultrasensitive Electrochemical Biosensor for Nucleic Acid Detection Based on Silver Nanoflower-Stem-Loop Probes
abstract: Nucleic acids are critical biomarkers that provide essential information throughout disease progression, making their detection critical to early diagnosis of both infectious and non-infectious diseases. However, existing detection methods, including classical analytical techniques and even most reported biosensors, are often constrained by complex procedures, high costs, and limited sensitivity, with the majority operating at the femtomolar level and failing to achieve single-molecule detection needed for early-stage diagnosis. Here, we report an electrochemical biosensor based on silver nanoflowers (AgNFs) integrated with stem-loop probes (SPs) for universal nucleic acid detection, using Norovirus RNA as a model target to validate the platform. The SPs serve as critical elements in a signal amplification system, converting target binding into a biotin–streptavidin recognition event, which leads to the accumulation of AgNFs-SP complexes on laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrodes and generates a strong electrochemical signal. Under optimized conditions with a 50 min hybridization incubation (total assay time ~60 min), the sensor exhibits a linear response to Norovirus RNA concentrations from 1 aM to 10 fM, with a measured detection limit of 1 aM, achieving single-molecule-level detection capability. abstract_zh: 核酸是疾病进展过程中的关键生物标志物,可提供重要信息,因此在早期诊断传染性和非传染性疾病方面,其检测至关重要。然而,现有检测方法(包括经典分析技术和大多数报道的生物传感器)常受限于复杂的操作流程、高昂成本和有限的灵敏度,大多数检测方法的灵敏度仅能达到飞摩尔水平,无法实现早期诊断所需的单分子检测。本研究报道了一种基于银纳米花(AgNFs)与发夹探针(SPs)集成的电化学生物传感器,用于通用核酸检测,并以诺如病毒 RNA为模型靶标验证该平台。发夹探针作为信号放大系统的关键元件,将靶标结合转化为生物素-链霉亲和素识别事件,进而导致AgNFs-SP复合物在激光诱导石墨烯(LIG)电极上积累,并产生强电化学信号。在优化条件下,杂交孵育时间为50分钟(总检测时间约60分钟)时,传感器对诺如病毒 RNA浓度在1 aM至10 fM范围内呈线性响应,检测限为1 aM,实现单分子水平检测能力。若需更快速检测,将杂交孵育时间缩短至20分钟(总检测时间约30分钟)时,线性范围转移至0.1 fM–1 pM,检测限为0.1 fM,在不要求最高灵敏度时提供更快速的定量检测。该生物传感器成本效益高、便于小型化,并被设计为可通过简单修改探针序列适配其他核酸靶标的通用平台,在多种疾病的早期诊断中展现广阔应用前景。

title: Living with Primary Immunodeficiencies: CVID—Enteropathy from the Perspective of a Gastroenterologist
abstract: Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), the most prevalent symptomatic primary antibody deficiency (∼1:25,000), in its symptomatic spectrum reaches way beyond intractable, chronic, and recurrent infections. Noninfectious enteropathy (CVID-E)—affecting 15–30% of patients—has emerged as a pivotal manifestation of the natural disease trajectory, with approximately 11-fold increased mortality risk. CVID-E is pathologically determined by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and abundant CD8+ T cell infiltration—yielding the phenotype that often mimics celiac disease. There are three pathogenic determinants that have been elucidated so far. First, almost absent mucosal IgA is permeating and facilitating gut pathogen expansion. With this process, gut membrane lipid metabolism is shifted toward inflammatory cascades, which may render an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-like phenotype. Second, a mixed and specific type I/III and type II interferon release drives CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity and macrophage recruitment, producing a graft-versus-host-like mucosal damage pattern yielding apparent villous injury. Third, chronic norovirus infection further augments this interferon-driven pathway, leading to high-grade epithelial damage even in early-onset disease. USIDNET registry analysis (n = 1,415) confirmed that CVID-E patients exhibit significantly lower performance status, higher rates of concomitant autoimmunity (30.7%), granulomatous disease, and even malignancy. Treatment is largely empirical with limited evidence-based data. Immunoglobulin replacement does not mitigate symptoms of enteropathy, and although corticosteroids restore architecture, they impose prohibitive infectious risk. Although TNF-α blockers and thiopurines achieved complete remission in select patient cohorts, overall therapeutic response was unsatisfying. Molecular medical tactics—employing JAK inhibitors targeting the interferon-specific pathways, namely abatacept for CTLA-4-related dysregulation—represent the most promising tool. CVID-E is a complicated disorder because it stands at the very intersection of immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology where these determinants encompass collapsed humoral defense, gut dysbiosis, and unbalanced interferon-driven epithelial necrosis converge. Multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics are urgently needed to supersede the current empirical interventions with a fully evidence-based approach.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of norovirus in the pathogenesis of CVID-E, a noninfectious enteropathy associated with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID). CVID-E is characterized by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and CD8+ T cell infiltration, often mimicking celiac disease. The review highlights three pathogenic determinants: mucosal IgA deficiency leading to gut pathogen expansion, interferon-driven immune responses causing mucosal damage, and chronic norovirus infection exacerbating these pathways. Despite the potential of JAK inhibitors and abatacept, current treatments remain empirical with limited evidence-based data. The review emphasizes the need for multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics to address the complexities of CVID-E, which involves immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 常见变异型免疫缺陷(CVID),作为最常见的症状性原发性抗体缺陷(约1:25,000),其症状谱远超难以治愈、慢性且反复发作的感染。非感染性肠病(CVID-E)影响约15–30%的患者,已成为自然疾病进程中的关键表现,其风险约为11倍。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: USIDNET注册分析(n = 1,415)证实,CVID-E患者表现出显著较低的生存状态,同时并发自身免疫(30.7%)、肉芽肿性疾病甚至恶性肿瘤的发病率更高。亟需多中心随机对照试验和精准治疗来取代当前的经验性干预,以实现基于充分证据的治疗方案。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CVID-E的病理特征由绒毛萎缩、缺乏黏膜浆细胞以及大量CD8+ T细胞浸润所决定,这种表型常与乳糜泻相似。目前已阐明三种致病机制。首先,几乎缺失的黏膜IgA会渗透并促进肠道病原体的扩增。在此过程中,肠道膜脂质代谢向炎症级联反应转移,可能导致类似炎症性肠病(IBD)的表型。其次,一种混合且特异性的I型/III型和II型干扰素释放驱动CD8+ T细胞的细胞毒性作用和巨噬细胞募集,产生类似移植物抗宿主病(GVHD)的黏膜损伤模式,导致明显的绒毛损伤。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 免疫球蛋白替代治疗无法缓解肠病症状,尽管糖皮质激素能够恢复肠道结构,但会带来显著的感染风险。尽管TNF-α阻断剂和硫嘌呤类药物在某些患者队列研究中实现了完全缓解,但总体治疗效果仍不令人满意。治疗的治疗主要基于经验,缺乏基于证据的数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 分子医学策略——使用针对干扰素特异性通路的JAK抑制剂,例如用于CTLA-4相关失调的阿巴西普——代表了最有前景的治疗工具。CVID-E是一种复杂的疾病,因为它处于免疫缺陷、免疫失调和黏膜病理的交汇点,这些致病因素包括体液免疫防御崩溃、肠道菌群失调以及干扰素驱动的上皮坏死失衡。

title: VIProDesign: viral protein panel design for highly variable viruses to evaluate immune responses and identify broadly neutralizing antibodies
abstract: Motivation: Highly mutable viruses continuously evolve, with some posing major pandemic risks. However, standardized neutralization assays and up-to-date viral panels are often lacking, limiting evaluation of immunogens and identification of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Closing these gaps is essential for guiding effective countermeasure development. Results: In this study, we present Viral Protein Panel Design (VIProDesign), a computational tool for designing viral protein panels that address the high sequence diversity of rapidly evolving viruses. VIProDesign uses the Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) algorithm to select representative strains and applies the elbow-point method based on cumulative Shannon entropy to balance diversity and panel size. We used VIProDesign to generate optimized panels for Betacoronavirus, human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1), Influenza virus, Norovirus, and Lassa virus. The tool also supports customizable panel sizes, making it suitable for both resource-limited contexts and early-stage research. This flexible approach streamlines viral panel design across diverse pathogens. Although VIProDesign was originally developed for viral proteins, its underlying framework is broadly applicable to the selection of representative protein panels across diverse taxa, including bacterial species, toxins, and other biologically relevant protein families.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenges posed by highly mutable viruses, particularly the lack of standardized neutralization assays and up-to-date viral panels that hinder the evaluation of immunogens and identification of broadly neutralizing antibodies. This is critical for developing effective countermeasures against viruses that continuously evolve and pose major pandemic risks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study introduced VIProDesign, a computational tool designed to generate optimized viral protein panels for rapidly evolving viruses. The tool was applied to Betacoronavirus, human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1), Influenza virus, Norovirus, and Lassa virus, with a focus on human noroviruses and their associated disease.
analysis.methods: The methods involved using the Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) algorithm to select representative strains and applying the elbow-point method based on cumulative Shannon entropy to balance diversity and panel size. The tool was tested on various viral species, including Norovirus, to evaluate its effectiveness in generating representative panels.
analysis.main_results: VIProDesign successfully generated optimized panels for Betacoronavirus, HIV-1, Influenza virus, Norovirus, and Lassa virus. The tool supports customizable panel sizes, making it suitable for both resource-limited contexts and early-stage research. Its flexible approach streamlines viral panel design across diverse pathogens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the results as demonstrating the utility of VIProDesign in creating representative viral panels that address sequence diversity. The novelty lies in the application of the elbow-point method based on Shannon entropy to balance panel size and diversity, which is a new approach in viral protein panel design.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of standardized neutralization assays and up-to-date viral panels, which are essential for evaluating immunogens and identifying broadly neutralizing antibodies. This has direct implications for improving surveillance and response strategies against rapidly evolving viruses like Norovirus.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, which may not fully capture the practical implementation of VIProDesign. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are based on computational methods and do not include empirical validation from real-world applications.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces VIProDesign, a computational tool for designing viral protein panels that address the high sequence diversity of rapidly evolving viruses. The tool uses the PAM algorithm and the elbow-point method based on cumulative Shannon entropy to balance diversity and panel size. It was applied to Norovirus and other viruses, demonstrating its flexibility and utility in generating representative panels for immunological and virological research. The findings suggest that VIProDesign can improve the evaluation of immunogens and the identification of broadly neutralizing antibodies, which is crucial for developing effective countermeasures. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, limiting the confidence in its practical implementation. The evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the lack of empirical validation from real-world applications.

title_zh: VIProDesign:针对高变异病毒的病毒蛋白面板设计,用于评估免疫应答并识别广谱中和抗体
source_body_en: Motivation: Highly mutable viruses continuously evolve, with some posing major pandemic risks. However, standardized neutralization assays and up-to-date viral panels are often lacking, limiting evaluation of immunogens and identification of broadly neutralizing antibodies. Closing these gaps is essential for guiding effective countermeasure development. Results: In this study, we present Viral Protein Panel Design (VIProDesign), a computational tool for designing viral protein panels that address the high sequence diversity of rapidly evolving viruses. VIProDesign uses the Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) algorithm to select representative strains and applies the elbow-point method based on cumulative Shannon entropy to balance diversity and panel size. We used VIProDesign to generate optimized panels for Betacoronavirus, human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1), Influenza virus, Norovirus, and Lassa virus. The tool also supports customizable panel sizes, making it suitable for both resource-limited contexts and early-stage research. This flexible approach streamlines viral panel design across diverse pathogens. Although VIProDesign was originally developed for viral proteins, its underlying framework is broadly applicable to the selection of representative protein panels across diverse taxa, including bacterial species, toxins, and other biologically relevant protein families.

title: Development and epidemiological investigation of a TaqMan-based multiplex real-time quantitative PCR assay for simultaneous detection of five bovine viruses (BVDV, AKAV, BNoV, BEV, and BCoV)
abstract: Inroduction Infectious diseases caused by bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV), Akabane virus (AKAV), bovine norovirus (BNoV), bovine enterovirus (BEV), and bovine coronavirus (BCoV) significantly threaten the cattle industry, resulting in substantial economic losses. These pathogens often present similar clinical signs, such as diarrhea, vomiting, and reproductive disorders in pregnant cattle, and frequent covert or mixed infections further complicate accurate diagnosis. Therefore, rapid, sensitive, and field‐deployable diagnostic methods are essential for effective disease surveillance and control in the cattle industry. Methods In this study, we report for the first time the establishment of a TaqMan‐based real‐time quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay that enables simultaneous detection of these five bovine viruses. Multiple sequence alignment of conserved genomic regions was performed, and virus‐specific primers and probes were designed and optimized using Beacon Designer 7 software. Subsequently, a TaqMan‐based multiplex real‐time qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of BVDV, AKAV, BNoV, BEV, and BCoV. The established detection method was applied to 200 clinical samples collected from 10 farms in multiple regions of Jilin Province. Results The results showed that the detection rates for BVDV, AKAV, BNoV, BEV, and BCoV were 33.50%, 0.50%, 4.50%, 7.50%, and 12.00%, respectively. Mixed infections were detected in 9 samples co‐infected with two of the five pathogens, with an overall mixed infection rate of 4.50%. Compared with conventional PCR, coincidence rates were 100% for BVDV, AKAV, BNoV, BEV, and BCoV. Discussion These findings indicate that the TaqMan multiplex real‐time qPCR assay developed here demonstrates favorable specificity, sensitivity, and reproducibility. This assay enables efficient detection and surveillance of bovine viruses, offering a reliable technical tool for the diagnosis and control of corresponding viral diseases in cattle.

title: Viral gastroenteritis: Molecular epidemiology of human norovirus by RT-PCR at University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of Congo
abstract: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

INTRODUCTION Noroviruses (NoV) are non-enveloped, single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Caliciviridae and are 2 J. Gen. Mol. Virol. recognized as the leading etiological agents of acute viral gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide (Winder et al., 2022). They are responsible for a substantial proportion of sporadic and epidemic gastroenteritis cases across all age groups and contribute significantly to morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals (Troeger et al., 2017). Due to their low infectious dose, prolonged environmental persistence, and high transmissibility, NoV infections represent a major global public health concern (World Health Organization (WHO), 2024; Patel et al., 2009). Diarrheal diseases remain among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in children under five years of age, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Recent estimates indicate that AGE accounts for hundreds of thousands of childhood deaths annually, with the highest disease burden occurring in Africa and South Asia (Sarno et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2017). Following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines, the epidemiology of viral gastroenteritis has changed considerably, with norovirus emerging as the predominant viral cause of AGE in many regions worldwide (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022). In sub-Saharan Africa, norovirus infections represent an increasing public health challenge. Several studies conducted in Burkina Faso, Mozambique, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Gabon, and Cameroon have reported substantial prevalence rates among children presenting with acute diarrhea (Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Afework et al., 2022; Louya et al., 2019; Rönnelid et al., 2020; Tegegne et al., 2024). However, the true burden of norovirus infection in the region remains underestimated due to limited access to molecular diagnostic methods, inadequate laboratory infrastructure, weak surveillance systems, and underreporting of gastroenteritis cases. These challenges hinder accurate estimation of disease burden and the development of effective prevention and control strategies. In developing countries, poor sanitation, limited access to safe drinking water, overcrowding, and inadequate healthcare resources contribute substantially to the transmission of enteric viruses, including NoV (Rönnelid et al., 2020). In the Republic of Congo, only a limited number of studies have investigated the epidemiology of norovirus infections. A previous study conducted in Brazzaville reported a prevalence of approximately 27% among hospitalized children with acute diarrhea (Ndjangangoye et al., 2023). Nevertheless, available epidemiological data remain scarce and fragmented. In 2020, the Republic of the Congo experienced an increase in cases of acute diarrheal disease, particularly among children requiring hospital care. Globally, norovirus had already emerged as the leading viral cause of epidemic AGE following the widespread implementation of rotavirus vaccination programs. However, despite this epidemiological context, molecular epidemiological data describing circulating norovirus genogroups were unavailable in the Republic of Congo. Therefore, documenting norovirus circulation during this period represented an important public health priority and provided baseline epidemiological information for the country (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Lopman et al., 2022). Ideally, effective surveillance systems supported by routine molecular diagnostic testing would enable continuous monitoring of circulating norovirus strains, early detection of outbreaks, and implementation of evidence-based public health interventions. However, in the Republic of the Congo, routine laboratory diagnosis of norovirus is not widely available, and epidemiological surveillance remains limited. Consequently, information regarding circulating geno- groups, transmission patterns, and associated risk factors remains insufficient. This lack of epidemiological information may have important public health implications, including delayed outbreak detection, inadequate allocation of healthcare resources, reduced effectiveness of preventive inter- ventions, and limited preparedness for future vaccine implementation programs. Strengthening local epidemio- logical evidence is therefore essential for improving disease control strategies and informing national health policies. Therefore, the present study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of norovirus among children presenting with acute gastroenteritis at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. By addressing existing knowledge gaps, this study seeks to provide valuable epidemio- logical evidence to support norovirus surveillance, prevention, and control strategies in the Republic of Congo. MATERIALS AND METHODS Ethics statement This study was approved by the Health Sciences Research Ethics Committee of the Republic of the Congo (Reference No. 286/MRSIT/IRSSA/CERSSA). Written informed consent was *Corresponding author. E-mail: anicetboumba1974@gmail.com. Author(s) agree that this article remain permanently open access under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 International License obtained from the parents or legal guardians of all participating children before enrollment. Study population A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June 1 to November 1, 2020, in the Pediatric Emergency Department of the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo. The study population consisted of children aged between 28 days and 17 years presenting with acute gastroenteritis during the study period, regardless of their immunological status. Acute gastroenteritis was defined as the passage of three or more loose or watery stools within a 24-h period. Children younger than 28 days of age, those presenting with bloody or mucoid diarrhea, and those with chronic or prolonged gastroenteritis were excluded from the study. The inclusion of a broad pediatric age range (28 days to 17 years) was intended to provide a comprehensive assessment of norovirus circulation across the pediatric population attending the referral hospital. Although norovirus infections are more frequently reported among children under five years of age, older children may also contribute to transmission dynamics and disease burden. Sample collection Participants were recruited using a consecutive sampling strategy. All eligible children presenting during the study period were enrolled consecutively until the target sample size was reached. The sample size of 50 participants corresponded to all eligible patients recruited during the study period and reflected the logistical and financial constraints associated with molecular testing. Although relatively small, this sample provided preliminary epidemiological data on norovirus infections among children with acute gastroenteritis in Brazzaville. A structured questionnaire was administered to collect sociodemographic, environmental, and clinical information. Stool samples were collected from all enrolled participants and transported under appropriate conditions to the laboratory. Samples were stored at −80°C until molecular analysis. Molecular analyses were performed at the Molecular Biology Laboratory of the Marie Madeleine GOMBES Foundation in Pointe-Noire. RNA extraction RNA extraction was performed using the Stool Total RNA Purification Kit Dx (NORGEN BIOTEK CORPORATION, Canada), following the manufacturer's instructions. This method is designed for isolation and purification of high-quality total RNA from stool samples, and based on spin column chromatography using Norgen’s proprietary resin as the separation matrix. RNA extracts were stored at -20°C prior to NoV detection and genogroup identification. Detection of NoV RNA and genotyping by real-time PCR Detection and genogroup identification of norovirus were performed using the RealStar Norovirus reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) Kit 3.0 (Altona Diagnostics, Germany). This assay allows qualitative detection and differentiation of norovirus genogroups GI and GII. The assay differentiates genogroups GI and GII using genotype-specific primers and hydrolysis probes labeled with distinct fluorescent dyes. Detection of fluorescence in the GI channel alone was interpreted as GI infection, whereas fluorescence detected only in the GII channel indicated GII infection. Simultaneous amplification in both channels, Amona et al. 3 together with valid internal and external controls, was interpreted as a mixed GI/GII infection according to the manufacturer's instructions. Positive and negative controls provided by the manufacturer were included in each RT-PCR run to ensure assay reliability. In addition, the heterologous internal control included in the kit was used to monitor both nucleic acid extraction efficiency and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) inhibition. Amplification was carried out on a MIC qPCR thermocycler using the following thermal profile: reverse transcription at 55°C for 20 min, initial denaturation at 95°C for 2 min, followed by 45 amplification cycles consisting of denaturation at 95°C for 15 s, annealing at 55°C for 45 s, and extension at 72°C for 15 s. All molecular procedures were conducted according to established laboratory quality assurance procedures, including standardized operating protocols, equipment maintenance, contamination prevention measures, and validation of control reactions before interpretation of results. Statistical analysis Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software version 27.0.1. Categorical variables were expressed as frequencies and percentages. Associations between categorical variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test when appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using Student’s t-test. Statistical significance was defined as a p-value < 0.05. RESULTS Socio-demographic and clinical characteristics of the study population A total of 50 children presenting with acute gastroenteritis were enrolled in this study. The majority of participants were aged ≤ 5 years (80%), while children older than 5 years represented 20% of the study population. The sex distribution was balanced, with 25 females (50%) and 25 males (50%). Regarding socioeconomic status, more than half of the participants originated from low-income households, while two-thirds were exposed to poor hygiene conditions, which is consistent with the continuing sanitation challenges reported in several low- income countries (Okesanya et al., 2024; WHO, 2025). Clinically, fever was observed in 80% of participants, increased stool frequency in 86%, and signs of dehydration were reported in all enrolled children (100%) (Table 1). Prevalence and distribution of NoV genogroups Norovirus RNA was detected in 22 of the 50 stool samples analyzed, resulting in an overall molecular prevalence of 44%. Among the positive samples, genogroup GII was the predominant circulating strain and was detected in 16 of 22 positive cases (73%). Genogroup GI was identified in 4 cases (18%), while mixed GI/GII infections were observed in 2 cases (9%), demonstrating the co-circulation of multiple norovirus 4 J. Gen. Mol. Virol. Table 1. Characteristic Number (n) Percentage Age ≤5 years 40 80 >5 years 10 20 Sex Female 25 50 Male 25 50 Socioeconomic level High 5 10 Medium 18 36 Low 27 54 Hygiene conditions Good 17 34 Poor 33 66 Collective environment Yes 7 14 No 43 86 Symptoms Fever 40 80 Increased stool frequency 43 86 Dehydration 50 100 genogroups in the study population (Table 2). Association between clinical manifestations and genogroups Analysis revealed a statistically significant association between age group and norovirus genogroup distribution (p = 0.03). Children aged ≤ 5 years were more frequently infected with genogroup GII compared with older children. No statistically significant association was observed between norovirus genogroups and clinical manifestations, including diarrhea, vomiting, fever, stool volume, or dehydration (p > 0.05) (Table 3). These findings suggest that although genogroup GII predominates among younger children, the clinical presentation of norovirus infection remains largely similar across circulating genogroups. DISCUSSION Acute gastroenteritis remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among children worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where access to healthcare, safe drinking water, and adequate sanitation remains limited. In recent years, norovirus has emerged as the leading viral cause of acute gastroenteritis following the widespread implementation of rotavirus vaccination programs (Cates et al., 2022; Dakouo et al., 2024; Chilaúle et al., 2022; Lopman et al., 2022). In the present study, the molecular prevalence of norovirus infection among children presenting with acute gastroenteritis was 44%. This prevalence is higher than that previously reported in the Republic of the Congo by Louya et al. (2019) and exceeds estimates reported from neighboring African countries, including Gabon, Ethiopia, and Nigeria (Ndjangangoye et al., 2023; Manouana et al., 2021; Tegegne et al., 2024; Omosigho et al., 2025). The relatively high prevalence observed in this study may be attributed to differences in study populations, healthcare- seeking behavior, seasonal variations, environmental conditions, and the use of sensitive molecular diagnostic techniques. Furthermore, the higher prevalence may be explained by the fact that sampling was conducted during the 2020 diarrheal disease epidemic, when viral gastroenteritis activity was particularly intense. title_zh: 病毒性胃肠炎:在刚果共和国布拉柴维尔大学医院中心通过 RT-PCR 检测人 流行病学 分子 流行病学
source_body_en: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses (NoV) recognized as the predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville. This study aimed to determine the molecular prevalence of NoV among children presenting with AGE, identify the circulating genogroups, and evaluate associated sociodemographic and clinical factors. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled. Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups. Eighty percent were aged ≤5 years. The overall prevalence of NoV infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. Clinically, fever was reported in 80% of cases, increased stool frequency in 86%, and dehydration was observed in all participants (100%). A significant association was observed between age and NoV genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years. However, clinical manifestations did not differ significantly between genogroups (p > 0.05). Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. Socioeconomic conditions and inadequate hygiene practices appear to play significant roles in NoV transmission.The integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures are recommended to improve prevention and control strategies. Key words: Norovirus, acute gastroenteritis, molecular epidemiology, reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), Congo.

title: Host genetic determinants of rotavirus disease and immunity in African children
abstract: Rotavirus (RV) is a major cause of diarrhoeal disease and mortality in African children. The impact of RV vaccination on child health has been limited by low vaccine effectiveness in resource-constrained settings. We urgently need better vaccines to control RV disease, delivery of which will require an improved understanding of RV biology. We hypothesised that the genetics of RV disease and immunity are likely to be mutually informative of RV biology. We performed genome-wide association studies of infection-induced and vaccine-derived RV immunity, hospitalised RV gastroenteritis (RVGE) risk and all-cause diarrhoeal disease risk in > 3,000 Ugandan, Kenyan and Zambian children. In doing so, we expand on the role of human blood group antigen secretion in RV infection and immunity, resolving complex interactions between secretor status, ABO blood group, Lewis antigen and viral genotype. We further identify a separate, novel locus at chromosome 2q12, rs59241810:T, associated with increased anti-RV IgA responses and lower risk of RVGE and all-cause diarrhoea with dehydration. Variation at rs59241810 regulates monocyte LIMS1 expression, thereby impacting IFNγ-induced hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) secretion, suggesting a role for monocyte-derived HGF in the generation of anti-RV IgA responses. Our data reveal the complex interplay between immunity, disease, pathogen variation and host genetics in RV infections, and identify LIMS1/HGF signalling as a target to design more effective anti-RV vaccines.
